name: No True Scotsman
shortDef: Redefining a group to exclude a counterexample instead of revising the claim.
definition: Defending a sweeping claim about a group by declaring, once a counterexample appears, that the counterexample was never a "real" or "true" member, so that nothing could ever count against the claim.
howToSpot: Did a counterexample appear just before the group got redefined?
Was the "real member" condition stated beforehand, or invented on the spot?
Is membership now defined by fitting the claim itself?
classicExample: No real fan leaves before the final whistle. Your brother left early? Then he was never a real fan.
legitimateVersion: Excluding a case is fair when it fails a definition that was set beforehand and is widely agreed, like pointing out that a "vegan" cupcake made with butter isn't vegan.

contrast.fal_special_pleading: No true Scotsman changes who counts as a member; special pleading keeps the rule but exempts one case from it.
contrast.fal_moving_the_goalposts: No true Scotsman redefines a group to dodge a counterexample; moving the goalposts raises the bar for proof after it was met.
